reviews.reasoning: Re-derived from both witnesses. Ps 56 is a shift+1 psalm, so the span web:Ps.56.1-Ps.56.7 = oshb:Ps.56.2-Ps.56.8 and the title pseudo-ref pairs web:Ps.56.0 = oshb:Ps.56.1 exactly as the row states. Every label the device note claims is present in the title bytes at oshb:Ps.56.1 (5 items: lamnatseach, the al-yonat-elem tune, le-David, miktam, and the historical clause). The WEB historical note at web:Ps.56.0, the trust-declaration quote at web:Ps.56.4, and the conspiracy quote at web:Ps.56.6 are all verbatim WEB (check_web_quotes over this cluster: 25 quotes checked, 1 flag, the unbound one below). Tiling over this cluster's 3 psalms is exact: 35 of 35 WEB verses, no gaps or overlaps. Selah silence is correct rather than an omission: the inventory carries 2 selah verses in Ps 56-58, both in Ps 57, and 0 verses in Ps 56, so there is nothing for this row to disclose. Three defects follow, none of them fatal to the span. I also weighed the refrain-lattice rival — a seam at web:Ps.56.4|56.5 closing the strophe on the trust formula, which is exactly how this cluster treats the Ps 57 refrain at web:Ps.57.5|57.6 — and did not file it: on the bytes Ps 56's return is split across two verses and reworded (a dropped pronominal suffix, an added divine name, one lexical swap), which is materially weaker as an edge marker than Ps 57's whole-verse return, and the row's chosen seam has an independent scene shift to divine record-keeping at web:Ps.56.8. Recorded as an observation, not a challenge: the rejected_alternative rebuts a rival nobody proposed (isolating one verse as its own row) and so leaves the real rival unanswered under a high confidence.

challenges.claim: The row quotes the WEB rendering of a ketiv/qere verse, web:Ps.56.6 = oshb:Ps.56.7, without the K/Q disclosure that quoting a K/Q verse triggers, and the quoted words are precisely what the qere carries.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.56.7 stages the pair inside the verse text itself: unpointed ketiv יצפינו followed by pointed qere יִצְפּ֗וֹנוּ, both spliced from oshb:Ps.56.7 and both byte tier against it (the ketiv is staged unpointed in the verse bytes). pmarks_Ps.json lists this verse in the K/Q inventory (kq at oshb:Ps.56.7 = 1 note; sweep: 65 K/Q verses book-wide, 68 notes). The row's observed_substrate_signals quotes “They conspire and lurk, watching my steps” (web:Ps.56.6) and its rationale ranges over web:Ps.56.5-Ps.56.7; “lurk” renders the qere, and web:Ps.56.6 = oshb:Ps.56.7 by the shift+1 arithmetic. No K/Q note appears in any field of the row.

challenges.claim: A curly-quoted WEB string in device_notes carries no web: ref in its field, the binding form the campaign makes mandatory at every layer; the campaign's own Tier-0 checker flags it.
challenges.evidence: check_web_quotes.py over this cluster returns quotes_checked 25, flag_count 1, at [0].device_notes: 'curly quote with NO web: ref in its field'. The string is genuine content, not a fabrication - the tune name “Silent Dove in Distant Lands” is byte-identical to the run WEB carries in the title at web:Ps.56.0 - so only the binding is missing, and the cure is adding the ref the other fields already use.

challenges.claim: device_notes states the al-tashcheth tune as shared by Psalms 57-59, but the byte-swept label membership is four psalms, and the statement carries no swept digit.
challenges.evidence: psalm_device_inventory.json genre_label_membership.al_tashchet = [57, 58, 59, 75] (sweep: 4 psalms, unit = psalms, not verses); Ps 75 is omitted from the row's sharing set. The contrast the row draws with Ps 56's own tune label survives - genre_label_membership.al_yonat_elem = [56] (sweep: 1 psalm) - so the defect is the unswept and short membership statement, not the contrast it supports.

reviews.reasoning: The original-language core of this row is sound. Both Hebrew quotes are whole verses and both reach byte tier against the refs they cite (oshb:Ps.56.11 and oshb:Ps.56.12), the dual-cite arithmetic in refs is correct for a shift+1 psalm at all 3 pairs, and the substantive observation - a trust formula stated once at web:Ps.56.4 = oshb:Ps.56.5 and returning split across web:Ps.56.10-Ps.56.11 = oshb:Ps.56.11-Ps.56.12, with the divine name doubled and one lexical swap - re-derives exactly from the bytes. The quote/gloss pairing is honest: the row glosses the two swapped tokens and does not gloss what it does not quote. Medium confidence is well calibrated for a strophe whose refrain material sits interior at both ends. Two defects: the device note narrates the campaign's own document trail rather than the text, and the identity claim is stated without the tier that makes it true.

challenges.claim: device_notes cites the book strategy's refrain roster and narrates its own erratum report - register the campaign bans in row prose without exception - and the claim is now false, since the roster has been amended to include Psalm 56.
challenges.evidence: The field reads: 'that the book strategy's refrain roster (42-43, 46, 57, 59, 62, 67, 80, 99, 107) does not list for Psalm 56 - reported as an erratum candidate, not a merged row.' The strategy's register rule bans strategy-section citations, erratum narration, and file-order talk in row prose EVER, and its writer-wave errata section (installed 2026-08-12) now reads 'Ps 56 belongs in the refrain roster', byte-verified by the orchestrator, with the instruction to cite per member with collate tiers. The textual observation underneath is correct and should survive the rewrite verse-anchored, with no reference to any campaign document: the formula at web:Ps.56.4 = oshb:Ps.56.5 returns split across web:Ps.56.10 = oshb:Ps.56.11 and web:Ps.56.11 = oshb:Ps.56.12.

challenges.claim: The claim that the clause at oshb:Ps.56.12 repeats the trust clause of oshb:Ps.56.5 with one word swapped holds at skeleton tier only; at byte and accent_stripped tiers two of the eight tokens differ, and no tier is named anywhere in the row.
challenges.evidence: Token-wise splice: the last 8 tokens of oshb:Ps.56.5 against all 8 tokens of oshb:Ps.56.12 differ at 2 of 8 positions at byte tier and at 1 of 8 at skeleton tier (sweep unit: tokens). Position 0 is בֵּאלֹהִ֣ים (oshb:Ps.56.5) against בֵּֽאלֹהִ֣ים (oshb:Ps.56.12) - the second carries U+05BD METEG that the first lacks, 12 codepoints against 11, so accent_stripped, which retains meteg, differs too. Position 6 is the lexical swap the row names, בָשָׂ֣ר (oshb:Ps.56.5) against אָדָ֣ם (oshb:Ps.56.12). collate of the oshb:Ps.56.5 clause against the verse oshb:Ps.56.12 returns tier 'none'. Naming the tier ('consonantally identical apart from one lexical swap') repairs it without touching the quotes.

reviews.reasoning: Everything this row asserts re-derives. The refrain quote reaches byte tier against oshb:Ps.57.6 and its dual-cite (oshb:Ps.57.6 = web:Ps.57.5) is exact for a shift+1 psalm; the English gloss covers the same 8-token span as the Hebrew, so quote and gloss are synced. The title claims match the title bytes at oshb:Ps.57.1 - lamnatseach, the al-tashcheth tune, le-David, miktam, and the cave note - and the opening row carries web:Ps.57.0 = oshb:Ps.57.1 in the mandated form. The selah handling is the one place in this cluster where 'interior' is byte-accurate: at oshb:Ps.57.4 = web:Ps.57.3 the selah token סֶ֑לָה (oshb:Ps.57.4) stands 6th of 10 tokens with 4 tokens following it, and WEB agrees, “he rebukes the one who is pursuing me. Selah. God will send out his loving kindness and his truth.” (web:Ps.57.3). The claim is inventory-true (pmarks selah at oshb:Ps.57.4) and is carried as corroboration only - the driver is the refrain, which is what the policy requires. Every out-of-span verse argued in prose is in refs (check_refs_mirror GREEN, 0 flags), and no pe/samekh, LXX, or tier-4 material appears anywhere. High confidence is earned: the closing edge is a whole-verse refrain whose return at oshb:Ps.57.12 is byte-verified. Two observations, neither filed: calling the single token הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם (oshb:Ps.57.6) 'the refrain' is loose, since the refrain is the whole verse and that token is only its distinguishing word; and 'outside this part's scope' in device_notes reads as work-unit talk under the register rule, though it is charitably readable as a section of the Psalter, which is why I leave it as an observation.

The collation work behind this row is right: the closing quote reaches byte tier against oshb:Ps.57.12, the article difference against oshb:Ps.57.6 is real and is the only token-level difference between the two refrain verses, and the doublet's WEB span is stated correctly (web:Ps.57.7-Ps.57.11 = oshb:Ps.57.8-Ps.57.12). I do not contest the span: the refrain-closed edge at web:Ps.57.5 is the better tier-1 edge on offer here - a whole-verse refrain whose return is byte-verified at oshb:Ps.57.12, against 2 seg-layer selah verses. But the selah fact is wrong in both witnesses, the row states no WEB arithmetic for either MT verse it quotes, and it names a campaign artifact in prose. One further observation, not filed: 'one word thinner' is not what the bytes show - both refrain verses carry 8 tokens in the maqaf-free staging, and the difference is a definite-article prefix (he plus patah, plus dagesh in the following shin, 3 codepoints), not a dropped word; the signal line's own 'one word differs' is the accurate formulation and already sits in the row.

challenges.claim: The selah at web:Ps.57.6 = oshb:Ps.57.7 is verse-final in both witnesses, but the row calls it an interior Selah that interrupts the verse and opens the strophe's second image.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.57.7 carries 11 tokens and its selah token סֶֽלָה is the 11th and last, with 0 tokens after it; WEB agrees at web:Ps.57.6, “They fall into the middle of it themselves. Selah.” The genuinely mid-verse selah of this psalm is the other one: at oshb:Ps.57.4 the token סֶ֑לָה stands 6th of 10 with 4 tokens after it, which is what the row covering web:Ps.57.1-Ps.57.5 correctly describes. The inventory records exactly 2 selah verses across this cluster's three psalms (pmarks selah at oshb:Ps.57.4 and oshb:Ps.57.7; 0 verses in Ps 56 and 0 in Ps 58; sweep: 71 selah verses book-wide). Corrected, the fact cuts against the use the row makes of it: a verse-final selah at web:Ps.57.6 corroborates a seam after that verse, not an interruption inside it - corroboration only, never a driver, which is why the span still stands on the refrain.

challenges.claim: Ps 57 is a shift+1 psalm and this row quotes Hebrew from oshb:Ps.57.12 and oshb:Ps.57.6, but no field of the row states the WEB arithmetic for either verse - its refs carry web:Ps.57.5 and web:Ps.57.11 bare.
challenges.evidence: boundary_evidence_refs = ['web:Ps.57.5', 'web:Ps.57.6 = oshb:Ps.57.7 (Selah)', 'web:Ps.57.7', 'web:Ps.57.11']: the selah pair is the only dual. The row covering web:Ps.57.1-Ps.57.5 states the same psalm's arithmetic inline, so this is a one-field cure.

challenges.claim: device_notes names a campaign artifact inside row prose, which the register rule bans.

reviews.reasoning: The crux handling is the best thing in this row and I would not disturb it: the term at oshb:Ps.58.2 is spliced byte-true, WEB's rendering is quoted verbatim at web:Ps.58.1, and the row declines to resolve the lexeme, which is the correct posture for a held zone. The title claims match the bytes at oshb:Ps.58.1, which carries 4 tokens and no historical clause. The defect is the closing edge: the row closes its span on a signal that opens material rather than closing it, and says so in its own rationale. Separately, check_universals flags 'with no historical note' in device_notes as an unswept negative; I do not file that, because it is a span-local negative about a single title that is byte-true from the 4 tokens of oshb:Ps.58.1, not a book-wide universal - reporting it as a checker false-positive class rather than a row defect.

challenges.claim: The row's own stated driver - the shift to imperative petition at web:Ps.58.6 - is an opener used as a closer; the tier-1 warrant sits one verse earlier at the seam web:Ps.58.5|58.6, and the span as drawn swallows the first verse of the petition block.
challenges.evidence: web:Ps.58.6 = oshb:Ps.58.7 by shift+1 arithmetic. oshb:Ps.58.7 opens on the vocative divine name אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים followed immediately by הֲרָס, and it is the only verse in the psalm that opens on a divine name (sweep over the 12 MT verses of Ps 58: 1 verse, oshb:Ps.58.7; unit = verses). WEB agrees at web:Ps.58.6: “Break their teeth, God, in their mouth. Break out the great teeth of the young lions, Yahweh.” - two imperatives and two vocatives, the addressee turning from the judges of the opening question to God. The verse the row would rather end on is not an independent close at all: oshb:Ps.58.6 opens אֲשֶׁ֣ר, a relative particle, and WEB renders web:Ps.58.5 “which doesn’t listen to the voice of charmers, no matter how skillful the charmer may be.” - a subordinate clause completing the cobra image of the verse before it. So the description block closes cleanly at web:Ps.58.5 and the petition runs web:Ps.58.6-Ps.58.11. Corroboration only, seg layer and single-witness: the psalm's only paseq stands in that same verse (pmarks paseq at oshb:Ps.58.7 = 1, and 1 of 1 in Ps 58). The row's own rationale concedes the shift is at web:Ps.58.6, and the row covering web:Ps.58.7-Ps.58.11 says the petition was 'opened at web:Ps.58.6' while excluding that verse - one edit on the shared seam at web:Ps.58.5|58.6 cures both rows.

challenges.claim: The signal line's statement that the debated vocative at oshb:Ps.58.2 opens the psalm is imprecise on both counts, and 'vocative' pre-resolves a syntactic reading the row says it is holding open.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.58.2 opens on the interrogative הַֽאֻמְנָ֗ם and only then the crux term אֵ֣לֶם (both spliced from oshb:Ps.58.2, byte tier), so the term is the second token of its verse; and its verse is not the psalm's first, since the counted title oshb:Ps.58.1 = web:Ps.58.0 is MT verse 1 and is tier-1 opener evidence in its own right. The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so the syntactic role cannot be machine-verified; the pointed bytes support either a vocative address or an adverbial reading, and WEB's “silent ones” (web:Ps.58.1) selects the first. Holding the lexeme open while fixing the syntax is half a crux.

reviews.reasoning: The closing warrant is right and I verified it on the Hebrew the row does not quote: the reported-speech frame at web:Ps.58.11 = oshb:Ps.58.12 opens וְיֹאמַ֣ר אָ֭דָם (oshb:Ps.58.12), a verb-plus-subject frame that cannot stand detached, so the rejected_alternative's refusal to close at web:Ps.58.10 is correct. The WEB image run is quoted verbatim and the imagery sequence is accurate verse by verse. The front seam is the problem, and it is the same seam contested on the row covering web:Ps.58.1-Ps.58.6. Observation, not filed: this row carries 0 original-language citations in a shift+1 psalm, and its discourse-frame warrant is argued from the English alone where the Hebrew frame at oshb:Ps.58.12 is the stronger evidence - not a defect under the letter of the rule, since the row makes no original-language claim, but it leaves the one piece of support for its own closing edge unused.

challenges.claim: The row names its driver as the imperative petition opened at web:Ps.58.6, but its span begins at web:Ps.58.7 - the driver sits outside the span, and the row's own first verse carries no opener.
challenges.evidence: The span is web:Ps.58.7-Ps.58.11 = oshb:Ps.58.8-Ps.58.12 by shift+1 arithmetic, while the petition's opening verse is web:Ps.58.6 = oshb:Ps.58.7, whose first token is the vocative divine name אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים (oshb:Ps.58.7) - the only verse in the psalm opening on a divine name (sweep over the 12 MT verses of Ps 58: 1 verse; unit = verses). The row's first verse opens “Let them vanish like water that flows away.” (web:Ps.58.7), a jussive image continuing that petition, and oshb:Ps.58.8 opens יִמָּאֲס֣וּ (oshb:Ps.58.8), a verb; its 10 tokens carry 0 divine names and no addressee shift. Moving the shared seam to web:Ps.58.5|58.6 gives this row a first verse that carries its own tier-1 driver; per seam-pair discipline this is one edit installed on both rows.

challenges.claim: The row quotes from a ketiv/qere verse, web:Ps.58.7 = oshb:Ps.58.8, with no K/Q disclosure.
challenges.evidence: pmarks_Ps.json records the note at oshb:Ps.58.8 (kq = 1 note; sweep: 65 K/Q verses book-wide), and the staged verse carries the pair in its own text: unpointed ketiv חצו followed by pointed qere חִ֝צָּ֗יו, both spliced from oshb:Ps.58.8. WEB renders the qere in the second half of the verse, “When they draw the bow, let their arrows be made blunt.” (web:Ps.58.7). The row quotes that verse's opening clause and paraphrases the rest of it without disclosure. Rated lower than the parallel case at web:Ps.56.6 = oshb:Ps.56.7 because here the quoted words are not the K/Q token itself.
